note: Generic owner step for every writable bind volume, replacing the per-volume elasticsearch_data_init and wiki_static_init. A fresh directory under runtime/volumes/ belongs to the host user, so on a Linux or WSL2 host a non-root writer cannot use it unless the host uid happens to match (redis is uid 999, the others 1000). `compose render` fills `volumes` and `command` from the profile (compose.with_owner_init): each volume goes to the `user:` of the services that mount it writable, and those services wait with service_completed_successfully. Services that keep root (the `user` control in manifest/hardening.json) never decide an owner: postgres, mongo and rabbitmq keep theirs, while unoconv shares wb_tmp with its uid-1000 writers and waits for this step. It runs the postgres image, which every profile has, because the step needs GNU coreutils: the elasticsearch2 base ships uutils chown, which returned 0 without changing another uid's private directory (measured). Explicit root (run_as 0:0) with cap_drop ALL and only CAP_CHOWN, read-only root, no-new-privileges, one hardening exception. A chown that has no effect stops the step, except on a VM share listed in compose.OWNERSHIP_IGNORING_FILESYSTEMS, where volume_access_check_* proves the writers can write. Every run walks the whole volume, so a stopped run is finished by the next one (SPEC-02 §4).
